items.title: The locus where a finite presentation module is flat in dimensions at least n is representable by a monomorphism of finite presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-flat.tex (Flatness on Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-flat.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's theorem at source lines 2195-2203, the main representability result of the chapter: for a morphism of finite presentation and a pure module of finite presentation, the functor classifying the points where the module is flat in dimensions at least n is an algebraic space and a monomorphism of finite presentation over the base. The 104-line proof (2205-2308) is a genuine research-level argument rather than a routine reduction: it first uses the sheaf property and the monomorphy to reduce representability to producing one surjective etale cover, then descends to schemes and uses the local nature of the question in the etale topology; after that it runs a descending induction on n, in which the induction hypothesis gives a quasi-finite base change to which purity is preserved, reducing to the case where the module is flat in dimensions at least n+1; finally it uses the existence of a complete devissage in an etale neighbourhood to shrink to a quasi-compact open W, proves that the set of points whose associated primes lie in W is constructible and contains a neighbourhood of the given point (via purity along the fibre and constructibility of the relative assassin), reduces to a finite disjoint union of the W_j, and quotes the flat case. Neither the induction nor the constructibility step is recorded in the statement.
